title: idol: one photo becomes a 3D model

facts.method: tool's own README and repo page, read on the day of the plan
facts.limits: One boundary: it makes single objects — your sneaker, your mug, your product — not whole rooms. Everything your photo shows, you still get.

scenes.heading: ONE PHOTO, NOW 3D
scenes.say: You shoot one photo for the product page — but can your buyer turn it around?

scenes.heading: PHOTO IN, 3D OUT
scenes.say: Drop one photo into idol — you pull out a full three-D model you can turn with your mouse. Even the sides your camera never saw are drawn in. In about two seconds.

scenes.heading: STRAIGHT INTO BLENDER
scenes.say: No studio, no turntable. It cuts the background, frames the object, and hands you a file that opens in Blender — so you drag it straight onto the product page or into a game.

scenes.heading: YOUR GPU, NOT THE CLOUD
scenes.say: Your own graphics card runs it — about seven gigabytes. No cloud call, no waitlist.

scenes.heading: ONE COMMAND
scenes.say: Or type one command on your own machine — python idol sample, photo.jpg — and your first model is done.

scenes.heading: PROOF ON ITS OWN TESTS
scenes.say: On the lab's own tests it beat both big image-to-three-D tools on every visual score — and it topped the trending list today.

scenes.heading: ONE BOUNDARY
nodes: you keep every angle you shot

idea: Drop one product photo into idol and you pull out a spinnable 3D model — no studio, your own GPU, one command.

claims.text: idol turns a single picture of an object into a full three-D Gaussian splat, including the sides the picture never showed, in about two seconds.
The pipeline removes the background, frames the object, and writes a standard 3DGS .ply that opens in Blender — no studio or turntable.
It runs on your own consumer GPU — 7.2 GB VRAM — with no cloud call or waitlist.
Try it free in the browser demo, or run one command on your own machine.
On the lab's own benchmark it edges TripoSplat and TRELLIS on every visual column, and it was the number-one trending model on Hugging Face today.
